open_obligations: Check whether expansion grows with student size, which would explain Burns et al.'s inverse scaling.
Note the theory's deterministic-teacher and robustness assumptions.
Do not treat the bound as quantitatively predicting Burns et al.'s agreement curves.
out.other_title: Inverse scaling of imitation: larger students agree less with weak supervisor errors
out.rationale: Burns et al. report larger strong students agree less with the weak supervisor's errors despite being trained to imitate it. Lang, Sontag and Vijayaraghavan prove a pseudolabel-correction bound showing student error on a class can be well below the teacher's error alpha_i when expansion from incorrectly to correctly labelled points is large and the student is robust; the theory covers deterministic pseudolabelers on a finite input space, not GPT-4-family finetuning.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: when a student trained on a weaker teacher's labels avoids reproducing the teacher's errors

text: The authors prove that if the family of robust non-mistake sets M'(S_i^good, F) satisfies (c, q)-expansion on (S_i^bad, S_i^good) with q < (3/4)(1 - 2 alpha), then any classifier f whose probability of disagreeing with the weak labels or being non-robust on S_i is at most (1 - alpha + 3c alpha)/4 has err(f, y|S_i) at most 2 alpha_i/(1 - 2 alpha_i) times its non-robust mass on S_i, plus err(f, weak labels|S_i), plus alpha_i(1 - 3c/2). They note this can be much smaller than the teacher's error alpha_i when c is large and the weak error and non-robust mass are small, unlike the trivial bound err(f, weak labels|S_i) + alpha_i.
title: Theorem 4.1: pseudolabel correction bound under expansion from bad to good labels
